title: High-Throughput Screening Model to Quantify Re-Epithelialization Kinetics
protocol: Grow low-passage epithelial cells to 70-80% confluence in 75 cm² tissue culture flasks.
Discard the growth culture media and wash the cells with 6 ml PBS.
Discard the PBS and add 2 ml trypsin/EDTA.
Incubate at 37°C for 3-5 minutes.
Add 8 ml of supplemented growth media into the flask.
Gently pipette up and down to resuspend the cells.
Take an aliquot of the cell suspension and determine the cell counts using a counting chamber.
Dilute Ca9-22 cell suspensions to obtain 3.5 x 10⁵ cells/ml in the corresponding growth media.
Dilute HO-1-N-1 and HaCat cell suspensions to obtain 3.0 x 10⁵ cells/ml in the corresponding growth media.
Mix the cell suspension gently.
Add 100 μl of the cell suspension into each well of a 96-well plate with flat bottom using a multichannel pipette.
Incubate for 16 hours in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO2.
Replace the growth media by 100 μl starvation media by aspiration of the culture medium without disturbing the cell monolayers.
Starve HaCat cells in keratinocyte serum-free medium (SFM).
Starve Ca9-22 cells in FCS-free DMEM/F12.
Starve HO-1-N-1 cells in FCS-free DMEM.
Optimize the duration and media used during starvation for each cell line.
Incubate the cells (Ca9-22, HO-1-N-1 or HaCat cells) for 2 hours in a humidified incubator at 37°C with 5% CO₂.
Prepare treatments for testing their effect on re-epithelialization kinetics in duplicates initially and with at least three technical replicates in refined studies.
Dilute all treatments in starvation media.
Prepare positive and negative controls as indicated.
Determine optimal concentrations of the controls by performing a titration for the target cell lines to achieve a large dynamic range between the positive and negative controls.
Exclude outer wells when preparing the master plate to avoid edge-specific artifacts such as evaporation of the medium.
Add 120 μl of each sample into the corresponding well on the master plate.
Prepare a solution of starvation media with fluorescent dyes.
Add 10 μl of Hoechst 33342 working solution into 5 ml starvation media to obtain a final concentration of 2 μg/ml.
Optionally, add 100 μl of CellTracker™ Red CMTPX stock solution into the mixture to obtain a final concentration of 2 μM.
Add the labelling solution into a reagent reservoir.
Aspirate the starvation media from the cells using a vacuum pump without disturbing the cell monolayer.
Add 50 μl of the labeling solution to each well.
Incubate at 37°C with 5% CO₂ for 20 minutes.
Incubate cells with the labelling solution for 20 minutes.
Perform a scratch in the cell monolayers of each well using the HTSScratcher.
Slide the plate under the 96-pin array and press towards the bottom of the wells.
Slide the array from left to right three times.
Release pressure from the array and remove the plate from the platform.
Rinse the array with water before each experiment.
Rinse the array with ethanol before each experiment.
Carefully aspirate the liquid from each well using the vacuum pump.
Wash the cells with 100 µl PBS.
Repeat washing step one more time.
Aspirate the PBS out of each well.
Transfer 100 µl of each sample from the master plate to corresponding wells in the assay plate using a multichannel pipette.
Add 100-200 µl PBS in the outer wells to avoid differential evaporation of samples.
Start image acquisition for Ca9-22 or HO-1-N-1 cell lines every 20 minutes for a total of 5 hours.
Adjust imaging intervals to 60 minutes for HaCat cell line and acquire images for 14-16 hours.
Rinse the array with ethanol after each experiment.
Download the virtual machine (VM) containing the Kinetic Re-Epithelialization Analysis Pipeline (KREAP) toolbox.
Import the VM into the player following the step-by-step instructions provided in the manual on the website.
Create an index file (.txt) and a compressed plate folder (.zip) containing the acquired images organized in separate folders for each well.
Upload the compressed folder and index file into the Galaxy history via the “Get data” tool.
Set the compressed folder’s type to .zip in the upload menu.
Run the KREAP Image Analysis tool to perform automated image segmentation.
Run the KREAP Data-Modeling tool to quantify re-epithelialization kinetics.
Set the time interval (minutes) between images in the index file.
